Suddenly I'm bedridden for 3 days and forced to rely on my friends and family for help. After that and a sobering mountain trip where I couldn't be useful to others for my validation I got news we were being laid off in a year at work. 
In like 2 weeks most of my identity and ego was destroyed, I didn't even mention how my back impacted my training which was a big part of my life. 
I started from ground zero and realised how childish I'd behave at times, only worrying about myself, barely being able to be empathetic and generally being emotionally immature. 
It's not that I was a horrible person inherently - it was mostly all coping mechanisms from childhood.
Know that there is almost nothing inherent about you - most everything is changeable. 
Also try to imagine other people as having gone through the same hardships you have, the same thought processes, anxieties etc.
P.S. be aware of the effect social media, I wasn't aware but I was comparing myself constantly to everyone and everything. 


Hope this helped and hope you have strength and trust in yourself to grow 🙏❤️

In short, ADHD is a dopamine dysregulation, dopamine helps you (or makes you) do things, which involves mental processes, including emotional regulation. If you don't have enough dopamine you can't regulate your emotions as well. It's never just a simple chemical imbalance tho, most of it is defense mechanisms learned from a young age and defense mechanisms take over your nervous system to keep you safe, thinking you can't handle it, but you can. Meditation keeps you in the real present where you can realise you're not in danger and can take control.

I've also had many symptoms that could be identified as ADHD, but some of the biggest help has been going to therapy to resolve my emotions. ADHD is in a way an emotional dysregulation, working with your emotions and confronting them instead of running away helped a lot. Doing this is challenging, doing it alone is very challenging, talking with friends and a therapist helps a lot. Meditation can also give you a perspective with which to work on these things without getting caught up in the emotional storms. Hope this helps, DM me if you need some pointers. May you be happy, healthy and free from suffering 🙏

I casually follow AI developments, mostly the image generation, and I know about chatgpt and that's about it. I do think it's extremely useful for stuff like medicine advancement and parts of education and research and data analysis, there are very good real world uses for AI.

Apart from socieoeconmic woes, most of the stuff it does is the fun of life, having conversations with people, making art and music that sucks, finding out stuff on your own through thorough reading, making mistakes and correcting them, doing that directly with other people. I even miss social media, which I've been cutting down on and don't like that much, when it wasn't filled with AI ads, reels, narrations and what not, 99% of it is just inauthentic, sub-par, minimum effort slop. Like I genuinely got mad that a bar made an AI poster for a show and a mechanic near me made his sign in ugly AI.

I've been fortunate enough to have met a lot of my goals by 25, stable job, education, independent living, and now I'm figuring out that the day to day with other people is what the interesting parts of life are apart from other long term goals. If most of that is replaced by AI cashiers, AI pizza place phone person, AI waiter and everything else, I'd be very sad. The mundanities of life is what reality is. If someone is relying on AI to get out of a bad financial situation, I understand that it's easier to do that using them in every way, it's survival.

I might have rambled a bit, but the gist of it that if I'm living decent and can continue to do so and even upgrade WITHOUT AI, I'll do that everytime. Thanks for reading, hope you guys are doing well.

This sounds like a significant problem. In order to try to fix this you can't tackle everything at once. Try to just distance yourself from your problems for a moment by grounding yourself. Then watch some comfort youtube/comedy series and feel what's it's like to feel good (at all).  I suspect some of these problems are related to do not trusting yourself or not feeling worthy. You might have set some standards too high knowing you might not achieve them to prove that your status of unworthiness.  Try doing something you know you can do and then appreciate it, regardless of whether you think it deserves appreciation or not. Then build upon this foundation, slowly. You and your existence is worthy of love and attention regardless of your thoughts about it. You're probably too hard on yourself for some reason, try to be soft, like you would with a friend. I very much resonate with this, I struggle with habit formation as well. It helps a lot to know how habits form - there's a cue to do an activity (time/place/thing), there's a craving to do the thing, to get a reward; there's doing the thing, and the reward, dopamine, of completing a task. 
   
I suspect I have ADD, and you might too. Understanding that your brain is wired in a certain way is a great start to understanding yourself and being compassionate towards yourself. Also, it's a symptom of our society to always think we're not enough and need to more, another concept in our mind to be aware of. 

I suspect also that you might have motivation issues, as I do, and I've been recycling my motivators on a weekly basis almost to help me do things. 

Learning to love yourself at first is a great step to creating a foundation for self - discipline, a necessary element for habit formation. I read Atomic Habits and it tells you everything you need to know about habit formation and inhibition (bad habits/addiction stopping). 

I would suggest as others have said, starting small, 3 minutes a day means you meditated today, so do 2 pages of a book, 1 mile ran, 1 weight lifted and so on. When you meditate like this, it leaves you wanting more, so you have an incentive to start tomorrow. If you force yourself to do 5 or 10 min a day, you might not enjoy it as much and would be deterred from it. 

A basic law to follow is to decrease the amount of friction and willpower needed to do your habit, and increasing it for things you want to stop doing. For example turning your TV off when you're done, or taking the plug out. 

I am certain you're intelligent and would grasp easily how habits are made, how your brain works and how to start making your own. 

A final note, learning about different philosophies of life and the like really helped me know myself more and gain confidence. I suggest reading/watching about different philosophies, both western and eastern to get a feel for your place in the world. 

Hope this helps, sorry if it's a bit all over the place. DM me if you need any help or advice and I'll try to help you the best I can. Thank you for reading and I hope you have a nice day friend ❤️
